podcasts.title: Ep 96: Nebius CTO on Racing the Hyperscalers Before AWS Wakes Up
podcasts.description: Nebius CTO Danila Shtan joins Jacob Effron to talk about what it takes to run an AI cloud at the frontier, and why he thinks the hyperscalers haven’t won this market yet. Today Nebius is a Nasdaq-listed AI cloud with infrastructure deals with Microsoft and Meta. Danila and Jacob discuss why open-model inference is still far from optimized, why 95% of Nebius customers run modified models instead of vanilla ones, and why prefill/decode disaggregation is more talk than practice. They also cover what’s actually constraining the AI buildout, why chip scarcity has kept AWS and Google from winning AI cloud, whether we’re overbuilding infrastructure, and how Nebius runs a large engineering org with no limits on AI token usage. He's led Redpoint's investments in companies like Abridge, Physical Intelligence & Legora. Follow Jacob on Twitter (@jacobeffron). On Unsupervised Learning we probe the sharpest minds in AI in search for the truth about what's real today, what will be real in the future and what it all means for businesses and the world. If you're a builder, researcher or investor navigating the AI world, this podcast will help you deconstruct and understand the most important breakthroughs and see a clearer picture of reality. podcasts.name: The Cognitive Revolution
podcasts.title: AI:AM: Carbon in the Arena, Mistral's Le Chonk, the Agent-Run Economy, Ferroelectric RAM + New Hacks
podcasts.description: Nathan Labenz and Prakash Narayanan examine whether prevailing AI assumptions survive real-world data across conversations with Anastasios Angelopoulos of Arena, Debo Olaosebikan of Kepler Computing, Samvit Ramadurgam of Union, Michael Freeman of ServiceNow, and Sagar Vaze of Mistral. The discussions evaluate production traces uncovering widespread model deception during extended tasks, ferroelectric memory engineered for older chip fabs, businesses run on tokens, and telemetry capturing AI-directed cyberattacks in Southeast Asia. These findings challenge conventional views on benchmark reliability, frontier compute efficiency, and the economic shift toward autonomous agents. In doing so, the episode directly tackles the critical stakes of whether dangerous capabilities can be contained once frontier models enter deployment.
